record: RCA Res. Ex. N° 127 (24 Feb 2020) approved a design drawing up to 169 L/s of groundwater from purchased rights in the Acuífero Santiago Central, a sector under restriction since 2005 and a prohibition zone since 1 Feb 2020. site_or_subject: Data Center Pecém (Casa dos Ventos; ByteDance reported client)
record: ANEEL had vetoed the connection in April 2025 on ONS advice citing transmission overload risk; ONS access opinions were reported on 29-30 May 2025 and ANEEL's authorisation for Data Center Pecém II (500 kV, future SE Pecém III) was published in the DOU on 26 Jun 2025 [press]. ONS letter CTA-ONS DGL 0815/2026 (8 Jun 2026) records that ANEEL Despacho 914/2026 granted Casa dos Ventos a precautionary measure keeping priority and capacity reserve for Data Center Pecém II; 300 MW initial, up to 900 MW; operations slated Jan 2027. Semace licensed phase 1 via a 658-page Relatório Ambiental Simplificado (31 impacts, 10 significant) classed low-impact; phase 1 210 MW average draw (5,040 MWh/day); water 18–30 m³/day via closed-loop air-cooled chillers, two SRH water-use permits, and an 18 Aug 2025 Cipp S/A–Utilitas reuse-water agreement replacing initially planned artesian wells. An MPF technical report (Laudo 1308/2025, Dec 2025) is reported to find that the licença prévia indicates 30 m³/day of groundwater while the SRH permits allow 88.24 m³/day; Semace said the permitted volume is a ceiling, not actual use [press]. On 22 Oct 2025 Idec, the Anacé people, Terramar and Frei Tito asked the MPF to suspend licensing and annul the licença prévia, citing lack of EIA/Rima and ILO 169 consultation. On 10 Sep 2026 the MPF and DPU filed Ação Civil Pública nº 0080626-66.2026.4.05.8100 against builder Omnia and Semace (State of Ceará and Caucaia later added), stating that the licença prévia and licença de instalação had been granted on an RAS, citing 300 MW installed power, ~70 ha and 120 diesel generators, and seeking to bar the operating licence and energisation pending ILO 169 consultation of the Anacé, an EIA/Rima and groundwater pumping tests.

record: Four projects total ~580 MW, about 34% of the City of Cape Town's current maximum demand of 1,676 MW (Daily Maverick calculation; the City did not comment). The City declined to release demand projections and backup-generator capacity citing POPIA. A 13 Apr 2026 objection by Foxglove and the Housing Assembly (Legal Resources Centre) to the Equinix rezoning cites undisclosed water volumes, generator numbers, diesel storage and possible Major Hazard Installation status; the City said in April 2026 it was still evaluating the application. The Municipal Planning Tribunal approved the Equinix rezoning for two data centres at King Air Industria (Case ID 1500156580) on 14 Jul 2026, with one member reported against. As reported from the written approval, a Site Development Plan must precede any building plan, and objectors' concerns about water, electricity, emissions and back-up generation were deferred to it [press]. The Legal Resources Centre estimates about 174 MW of demand; objectors' appeal was heard by the Planning Appeals Advisory Panel on 12 Oct 2026.

site_or_subject: Lagos data centers: on-site diesel and gas generation

Rack Centre's March 2025 media briefing (company-sourced Techpoint 'Brand Press' post) describes its 12 MW LGS2 as running on 'predominantly gas power, diesel and eventually solar', with gas turbines installed to complement diesel generators. Connecting Africa (Jun 2025) counts 17 data centers, 14 in Lagos (per DataCenterMap), cites a Mordor Intelligence estimate of ~136.7 MW for 2025, says gas gensets are the most common alternative (unnamed research) and that MTN reported 40% power savings from gas versus diesel (no primary source).
